result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Answer A frames almost every question as a named worker in a concrete floor situation, and its wrong options are believable mistakes. Each answer explains why the wrong options fail, though some of those explanations add consequences not in the session list (e.g., driving across a slope rolls the truck). Answer B's answers stick strictly to the list, but most questions just ask the hire to recite a rule, several have no wrong options at all, and its key only restates the rule without explaining why the tempting wrong choice fails. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): B turns every rule into a concrete floor scenario with plausible distractors, and explains why each wrong option fails. A is mostly recall questions with no explanations, and several of its questions have no options at all. B's rationales add a few points the session list doesn't cover, such as the claim that driving across a slope can roll the truck, the tipping explanations, and the extra next-steps advice, so it loses a little on item 2.
